production.name: production
production.description: In HSE, the production department refers to the area responsible for manufacturing, assembly, or processing of goods. Observations here often involve machine safety, process hazards, line stoppages, and worker behaviors on the shop floor. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe work practices, or exposure to hazardous materials during production activities.
examples: Operator bypassed machine guard during shift on the assembly line.
Spill of coolant observed near production equipment.
Worker not wearing hearing protection in the manufacturing area.
Conveyor belt emergency stop was blocked by materials.
Unlabeled chemical container found in the production zone.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.description: The maintenance department handles the repair, servicing, and upkeep of equipment and facilities. HSE observations here often relate to lockout/tagout procedures, working at heights, confined space entry, and tool safety. Incidents may involve improper isolation, slips during repairs, or missing PPE during maintenance tasks.
examples: Technician entered confined space without gas test in maintenance area.
Lockout/tagout procedure not followed during pump repair.
Oil spill left uncleaned after equipment servicing.
Missing guard on grinder in maintenance workshop.
Worker used ladder with damaged rung during maintenance task.

quality.name: quality
quality.description: The quality department oversees product standards, inspections, and compliance with regulations. HSE observations here may involve unsafe sampling practices, improper handling of test chemicals, or ergonomic risks during inspections. Events can include exposure to hazardous substances or unsafe storage of quality control samples.
examples: Inspector handled samples without gloves in quality lab.
Spilled solvent not cleaned up in QC area.
Ergonomic risk observed during repetitive testing procedure.
Blocked emergency exit in quality control office.
Unlabeled reagent stored in quality assurance cabinet.

logistics.name: logistics
logistics.description: The logistics department manages the movement, storage, and distribution of materials and products. HSE issues here often involve vehicle safety, manual handling, loading dock hazards, and traffic management. Observations may include unsafe forklift operation, blocked walkways, or improper stacking of goods.
examples: Forklift operated at excessive speed in loading area.
Pallets stacked unsafely in logistics zone.
Delivery truck blocked emergency access route.
Worker lifted heavy box without assistance in shipping area.
Spill of oil near loading dock not reported.

administration.name: administration
administration.description: The administration department covers office-based staff and support functions such as HR, finance, and management. HSE observations here typically relate to office ergonomics, fire safety, slips and trips, and emergency preparedness. Incidents may include blocked fire exits, poor workstation setup, or electrical hazards in office areas.
examples: Blocked fire exit in administration corridor.
Loose electrical cable caused trip hazard in office.
Improper chair height led to ergonomic complaint.
Unattended coffee spill in admin break room.
Emergency evacuation plan missing from administration area.

safety.name: safety
safety.description: The safety department is responsible for implementing and monitoring health and safety policies, conducting audits, and ensuring compliance. Observations here may include unsafe practices during safety inspections, missing signage, or gaps in emergency response readiness. Events often involve safety walkthroughs, training sessions, or incident investigations.
examples: Safety signage missing in high-risk area during inspection.
Fire extinguisher found discharged during safety audit.
Emergency drill not conducted as scheduled by safety team.
PPE compliance not enforced during safety walkthrough.
Incident investigation report incomplete in safety office.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description: The engineering department designs, modifies, and oversees technical systems, equipment, and processes. HSE observations here may involve design-related hazards, unsafe modifications, or risks during commissioning and testing. Events can include inadequate guarding on new equipment or lack of risk assessment for engineering changes.
examples: New machine installed without proper guarding by engineering.
No risk assessment conducted for process modification.
Temporary wiring left exposed after engineering test.
Engineering team entered restricted area without permit.
Design change increased manual handling risk.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: The warehouse department is responsible for storing raw materials, components, and finished goods. HSE issues here often involve manual handling, racking safety, slips and trips, and vehicle-pedestrian interactions. Observations may include blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Aisle blocked by pallets in warehouse.
Worker climbed racking to retrieve item.
Spill not cleaned up in warehouse storage area.
Forklift reversed without spotter in warehouse.
Damaged shelving reported in warehouse zone.

operations.name: operations
operations.description: The operations department oversees the day-to-day running of core business activities, often integrating production, logistics, and support functions. HSE observations here may cover cross-functional risks, process upsets, or coordination issues affecting safety. Events can include process deviations, communication breakdowns, or unsafe handovers between shifts.
examples: Shift handover missed critical safety information in operations.
Process deviation not reported to operations supervisor.
Operations team failed to isolate equipment before maintenance.
Unclear responsibilities led to unsafe condition during operations.
Operations staff not briefed on new emergency procedure.

facility_management.name: facility_management
facility_management.description: Facility management covers the upkeep, safety, and functionality of buildings and infrastructure, including utilities, cleaning, and groundskeeping. HSE observations here often involve building hazards, fire safety, contractor management, and environmental risks. Incidents may include blocked emergency exits, unsafe contractor practices, or poor housekeeping in common areas.
examples: Emergency exit blocked by cleaning equipment in facility corridor.
Contractor worked at height without harness in facility area.
Leaking pipe reported in facility management zone.
Poor lighting in facility stairwell created trip hazard.
Housekeeping standards not met in facility common area.
